tasks.title: A known-issues page that stays current
requirements: docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md lists every open issue labelled bug and every limit the docs state (a sentence carrying the marker <!-- limit -->), each with its link or page, the date it was first seen and the workaround if there is one

scripts/docs/known-issues.mjs --check reads the open issues through the GitHub API (or a file given with --issues, for tests) and the docs, and fails naming any open bug or stated limit the page lacks and any listed issue that is closed; CI runs it on a schedule and before a release
the README and the docs index link the page

--check reads the issues through the GitHub API with every page followed, takes the API base from MEMEV_GITHUB_API, fails naming the status on any answer but 200, and counts an issue absent from the open set as closed
an open bug that also carries the security label is never required on the page, and --check fails if the page shows its number or title
a workflow with a schedule and issues: read runs node scripts/docs/known-issues.mjs --check, and release.yml runs it before the release upload

the limits the docs state carry <!-- limit -->, at least README.md's Windows preview line, docs/INSTALL-FOR-AI.md's Windows line, docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md's line on two vaults and docs/CLIENTS.md's not-supported line, and the committed page passes --check against the repository's real issues

tasks.title: A three-day soak of the free tier
requirements: scripts/soak/free-tier.mjs runs one vault for 72 hours on one machine: the daemon, GitHub backup to a local bare repository, the hooks of two clients driven at a fixed rate (remember, recall, the prompt hook, session end), a daemon restart every 6 hours and a network drop every hour

it writes bench/results/<date>-soak-<cpu>.json with the hardware, the hours run, the notes written and found again, notes_lost, daemon crashes, the hourly p95 of the prompt hook and of recall, and the hourly heap and disk use
a 10-minute form (--minutes 10) runs in CI on a schedule, so the script cannot rot

the results file also records script_sha256, started_at, ended_at, the hourly samples, restarts, network_drops, write_errors, backup_failures and the daemon's RSS, and the short forms compress the restart and drop schedule in proportion
a run whose daemon crashes, that loses or fails a write, fails a backup or exceeds the bounds exits non-zero; found again means a recall hit whose body holds the written text
the soak runs in a sandbox of its own (HOME, MEMEV_CONFIG_DIR and XDG_CONFIG_HOME) and leaves no daemon running after it exits, normally or on SIGTERM

criteria.statement: SR-2.10 soak: the soak's one-minute form on a temp vault writes a results file with every field; a note deleted from the vault mid-run makes it report notes_lost 1 and exit non-zero

criteria.statement: The latest results file is consistent with a real run of the committed script: script_sha256 equals the sha256 of scripts/soak/free-tier.mjs; ended_at minus started_at is at least 72 h and equals hours; there are at least 72 hourly samples with strictly increasing timestamps; notes_written > 0 and notes_written == notes_found + notes_lost. A determined forger can still fake this; it stops the accidental and lazy cases

verifier.cmd: f=$(ls bench/results/*-soak-*.json | sort | tail -1) && node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),c=require("crypto");const r=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8"));const h=c.createHash("sha256").update(fs.readFileSync("scripts/soak/free-tier.mjs")).digest("hex");const s=Date.parse(r.started_at),e=Date.parse(r.ended_at);const H=r.hourly||[];const ok=r.script_sha256===h&&e-s>=72*3600e3&&Math.abs(r.hours-(e-s)/3600e3)<0.01&&H.length>=72&&H.every((x,i)=>i===0||Date.parse(x.at)>Date.parse(H[i-1].at))&&r.notes_written>0&&r.notes_written===r.notes_found+r.notes_lost;process.exit(ok?0:1)' "$f"

criteria.statement: The one-minute form compresses the schedule in proportion (restart every 6 h and drop every 1 h scaled by minutes/4320). The test asserts that the results report restarts >= 2 with a different daemon pid after each, network_drops >= 2 with a write made during a drop found afterwards, writes from both client ids, and backup_failures 0, and that git -C <bare> ls-tree -r HEAD contains every note written. A second run whose bare repository path is replaced by a plain file reports backup_failures > 0 and exits non-zero
